ai.description: Limborg’s Frog is a small species reaching 35–45 mm. It is brown with a distinct dark interorbital bar and a pale vertebral stripe. Males possess enlarged heads and prominent odontoid processes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Limnonectes limborgi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored supratympanic fold that extends from the eye to the shoulder, unlike similar species.
ai.habitat: Limborg's frogs inhabit leaf litter along small, clear streams within primary evergreen tropical forests, typically at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Limborg's frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small invertebrates along the leaf litter of forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: Limnonectes limborgi breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in terrestrial nests near streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Limnonectes limborgi* occurs in Northeast India (e.g., Mizoram, Meghalaya) within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot, typically inhabiting forests at low to mid-elevations.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Limnonectes limborgi* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from rocky streams in forest habitats.
